predecessors.name: Colchis
predecessors.text: Colchis, the Black Sea coast of western Georgia, which the Lazica page calls a 'state in West Georgia from about the 1st century BC'

successors.name: Kingdom of Lazica
successors.text: the Lazic kingdom in Cliopatria's 638-777 row, the same state

ledger.x: -63: Cliopatria's Lazica begins on the Black Sea coast of western Georgia.
306: Lazica's outline grows by about 6,400 km2 in Cliopatria.
528: the Persians hold Shorapani and Skanda.
532: the Eternal Peace returns what was taken.
541: Khosrow I enters Lazica and takes Petra; the Lazic War begins.
562: the Fifty-Year Peace ends the Lazic War.
637: bookkeeping hand-over to Cliopatria's Kingdom of Lazica row (638-777), which the Lazica page treats as the same kingdom.

wars.name: Revolt of Anicetus against Rome
wars.outcome: 'Between 69 and 79, a Laz admiral named Anicetus led his people in revolt against the Romans'; no change of land is recorded.

wars.name: Iberian War
wars.outcome: Persian forces held Shorapani and Skanda from 528; the Eternal Peace of 532 returned all seized territory and left Lazica to Byzantium.

wars.name: Lazic War
wars.outcome: Indecisive: Byzantium paid annual tribute to Persia in return for Persia recognising Lazica 'as a Roman vassal state'; 'the Sasanian Empire thus held a slight advantage'.

wars.name: Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628 (Heraclius's Caucasus campaigns)
wars.outcome: 'In the 620s, the Laz, together with the Abasgians, participated in Emperor Heraclius' campaigns'; no Lazic land change is recorded on the page.

certainty.note: The coastal limits to the south (Trabzon) are explicitly vague on the page ('did not extend its direct administrative control as far as Trabzon in the 4th century'); during the Lazic War the Petra-Archaeopolis fortress lines moved year by…
